title: Unit Legalization — Frequently Asked Questions | City of Halvern
text:
# Unit legalization: frequently asked questions

*Page last reviewed November 2024.*

**Who runs the program?**
The Planning Division accepts and screens unit legalization applications. Planning staff will route your application to Building for plan review.

**What does it cost?**
The application fee is $390. There is a separate inspection fee. Fees are set in the city's master fee schedule and are updated each fiscal year.

**Do I need an appointment before applying?**
No. You may submit a completed application at the Permit Center during counter hours, or mail it to the Planning Division.

**How long does it take?**
Plan on about 30 days from submittal to a decision if your application is complete and the unit does not need corrections.

**What if my unit was built after 2020?**
The amnesty program does not apply. You would need a standard building permit for the conversion, and the unit may be subject to code enforcement.

**Will the city report me to code enforcement if I apply?**
No. Marisol Government Code section 41210(h) bars the city from initiating an enforcement action based solely on an application filed under the amnesty program, unless the unit presents an immediate hazard.

**Can I sell the house while the application is pending?**
Yes, but the Certificate of Legalization is issued to the property, not the owner, and any outstanding corrections transfer with the parcel.

# City of Halvern — Master Fee Schedule FY 2025-26 (excerpt)

Adopted by Resolution No. 25-07; effective April 1, 2025. All fees are cost-recovery under Marisol Government Code section 41210(f), which provides that a fee adopted under this article shall not exceed the reasonable cost of providing the service.

| Service | Fee | Notes |

title: Ordinance No. 24-118 — Legalization of Existing Unpermitted Dwelling Units
text:
ORDINANCE NO. 24-118

AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF HALVERN ADDING CHAPTER 15.42 TO THE
HALVERN MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO THE LEGALIZATION OF EXISTING UNPERMITTED DWELLING
UNITS, AND AMENDING THE MASTER FEE SCHEDULE

Adopted March 11, 2025. Effective April 1, 2025. Supersedes Ordinance No. 22-041.

The City Council of the City of Halvern ordains as follows:

SECTION 1. FINDINGS. Marisol Government Code section 41210 authorizes a city to establish a
program for the legalization of dwelling units constructed without permits before January 1,
2020, and requires each participating city to designate an administering department, publish a
submittal checklist, determine the completeness of an application within 30 days, and provide
an appeal of a denial to the governing body.

SECTION 2. CHAPTER 15.42 ADDED.

15.42.030 Administering department. The Building Division shall administer this chapter.
Applications previously accepted by the Planning Division shall be transferred to the Building
Division upon the effective date of this ordinance.

15.42.040 Pre-application meeting. An applicant shall attend a pre-application meeting with a
plans examiner before an application is accepted. The Building Official shall publish meeting
availability and may waive the meeting in writing where the unit has a current, active building
permit history.

15.42.050 Completeness determination. Within 30 days of submittal the Building Division shall
notify the applicant in writing that the application is complete, or shall identify the items
required to complete it. Resubmittal restarts the 30-day period.

15.42.060 Inspection. The Building Division shall inspect the unit. Where the inspection
identifies noncompliance, the Division shall issue a correction notice and the applicant may
obtain permits to perform the corrections; the unit shall be reinspected upon completion.

15.42.080 Fees. The application fee and the inspection fee shall be as set in the master fee
schedule and shall not exceed the reasonable cost of administering this chapter.

15.42.090 Appeal. An applicant may appeal a denial to the City Council within 15 days of the
notice of denial.

title: Unpermitted Dwelling Unit Legalization Program | City of Halvern
text:
# Unpermitted Dwelling Unit Legalization Program

The Building Division administers Halvern's unit legalization program under Marisol Government Code section 41210 and Halvern Ordinance No. 24-118. The program lets an owner bring an existing unpermitted dwelling unit into compliance without the unit being red-tagged, provided the unit was constructed before January 1, 2020 and can be brought up to the standards in Chapter 15.42 of the Municipal Code.

## How to apply

1. **Schedule a pre-application meeting.** A pre-application meeting with a Building Division plans examiner is required before an application will be accepted. Meetings are held Tuesdays and Thursdays at the Permit Center, 411 Ridgeway Ave., 2nd floor. Call (555) 214-8890 or use the online scheduler.
2. **Submit Form BLD-214** with existing-condition floor plans, a site plan, and the legalization application fee of $430. Applications are accepted at the Permit Center counter or through the online portal.
3. **Application screening.** Permit Center staff review your submittal for completeness. Within 30 days of submittal you will receive either a notice that the application is complete or a completeness letter listing what is missing.
4. **Plan review.** A plans examiner reviews the application against the Building Code and Chapter 15.42. Most applicants receive one round of corrections. Corrected plans are resubmitted through the portal and re-enter plan review.
5. **Site inspection.** A building inspector inspects the unit. The inspection fee is $185, billed before the inspection is scheduled. Reinspection, if required, is $95.
6. **Certificate of Legalization.** When plan review and inspection are cleared, the Building Division issues a Certificate of Legalization for the unit.

## How long does it take?

Most complete applications are resolved in six to eight weeks from submittal. Applications that require corrections take longer. The 30-day period in step 3 is a completeness determination only; it is not a deadline for the final decision.

## Related pages

- Fee schedule: https://www.halvern.gov/finance/fee-schedule-2025
- Application form BLD-214: https://www.halvern.gov/forms/bld-214-unit-legalization.pdf
- Frequently asked questions: https://www.halvern.gov/building/unit-legalization/faq
- Ordinance No. 24-118: https://library.halvern.gov/ordinances/24-118

Questions: legalization@halvern.gov

title: Staff Report, Item 7 — Unit Legalization Program Update and Fee Amendment
text:
CITY OF HALVERN — CITY COUNCIL STAFF REPORT
Meeting date: March 11, 2025            Item 7
From: R. Okonkwo, Chief Building Official
Subject: Adoption of Ordinance No. 24-118 and amendment of the master fee schedule for the
unit legalization program

RECOMMENDATION
Adopt Ordinance No. 24-118, transfer program administration from Planning to the Building
Division, and set the application fee at $430 and the inspection fee at $185.

BACKGROUND AND CURRENT WORKFLOW
The program has operated since 2022 under Ordinance No. 22-041 with a $390 application fee.
Planning accepted applications; Building performed plan review. The split intake is the primary
source of delay identified in the Division's file review of 143 applications closed in FY 2023-24:

1. Counter intake and screening by Permit Center staff (median 4 calendar days).
2. Interdepartmental routing. Every application is circulated to the Fire Prevention Bureau and,
   where the unit is served by a private lateral, to Public Works for utility review. This step is
   not visible to applicants and adds a median of 9 days; 12 percent of files wait more than
   three weeks for Fire comment.
3. Plan review by a plans examiner (median 21 days to first comment). 35 percent of applications
   receive a correction notice and re-enter plan review after resubmittal.
4. Field inspection (median 11 days from request to inspection).
5. Second-level sign-off. The Chief Building Official reviews and signs every legalization
   approval. With one incumbent this step has queued at a median of 5 days and up to 18 days
   during vacation coverage.
6. Fee reconciliation by Finance before the certificate is released; understated inspection fees
   were invoiced late in 31 of 143 files.
7. Records archiving to the permanent parcel file (post-issuance, clerical).

PERFORMANCE
Median time from submittal to issuance, FY 2023-24: 47 calendar days. 90th percentile: 96 days.
Denial rate: 8 percent (11 of 143), almost all for units that could not meet egress or ceiling
height. Staff estimate the ordinance will reduce median time by 6 to 9 days by consolidating
intake and authorizing the plans examiner to sign routine approvals when the Chief Building
Official is unavailable.

FISCAL IMPACT
Full cost recovery requires $615 per application (3.5 FTE allocated, $212,000 program cost,
FY 2023-24 volume of 143). Staff recommend $430 plus $185 at inspection.

title: Sidewalk Vending Permits | City of Halvern
text:
# Sidewalk Vending Permits

Community Services issues sidewalk vending permits under Marisol Government Code section 51422 and Halvern Municipal Code Chapter 5.28. A permit is required to sell food or merchandise from a stationary or roaming cart on a public sidewalk.

## Steps

1. Complete Form CS-31 and attach a photo of the cart, a copy of your Marisol seller's permit, and, for food carts, a county health permit from Marisol County Environmental Health.
2. Pay the annual permit fee of $125 ($85 on renewal).
3. Cart inspection at the Community Services yard, 2120 Del Norte Road. Inspections are scheduled within 10 business days of a complete application.
4. Permit issuance. Staff issue the decal and the permit card at the counter.

Most complete applications are issued within 15 business days. Enforcement of vending violations is by administrative citation only; sidewalk vending is not a criminal offense in Halvern.

Food carts must also hold a Marisol County health permit before the city permit will be issued. The county process is separate and takes longer than the city process; start with the county.

title: Unpermitted Unit Compliance Program | City of Ardenmoor Planning Department
text:
# Unpermitted Unit Compliance Program

The Planning Department administers Ardenmoor's compliance program for existing unpermitted dwelling units under Marisol Government Code section 41210 and City Council Resolution No. 2024-32. The program applies to units constructed before January 1, 2020.

## Steps

1. **Submit the application.** File Form P-51 with existing-condition plans and the $275 application fee online or at the Planning counter, 90 Fairmont Street. No appointment is needed.
2. **Completeness review.** Planning staff notify you within 30 days whether the application is complete.
3. **Code review.** A planner reviews the application with the Building Official. Corrections, if any, are emailed to the applicant.
4. **Inspection.** You may choose either a city inspection at no additional charge, or an inspection by a licensed third-party inspector from the city's approved list at your own expense. Third-party reports are accepted if submitted on Form P-53 within 30 days of the inspection.
5. **Certificate of Compliance.** Planning issues a Certificate of Compliance when all corrections are cleared.

## Timeline

Applicants should expect 30 to 45 days from a complete application to a certificate. Choosing the third-party inspection option typically saves one to two weeks because city inspection slots are limited.

## Fee waiver

The application fee is waived for applicants at or below 80 percent of area median income. Submit Form P-49 with the application.

Contact: unitcompliance@ardenmoor.gov, (555) 770-3311

title: Sidewalk Vending FAQ | City of Ardenmoor
text:
# Sidewalk vending: frequently asked questions

**Do I need a permit to vend on an Ardenmoor sidewalk?**
Yes. Ardenmoor issues sidewalk vending permits through the Business Services counter under Marisol Government Code section 51422.

**What does it cost?**
$95 per year. There is no inspection fee. Food carts must hold a county health permit.

**How long does it take?**
Business Services issues permits within 10 business days of a complete application. There is no hearing and no plan review.

**Where may I not vend?**
Within 100 feet of a school entrance during school hours, in the Fairmont Street farmers market footprint on Saturdays, or in a park where a concession agreement is in effect.

**Is there a cap on the number of permits?**
No. State law prohibits a cap that is not based on objective health, safety, or welfare concerns.

**Can my permit be revoked?**
Yes, after a fourth administrative citation in a twelve-month period. Revocation may be appealed to the City Manager.

title: Unpermitted Structure Legalization | Marisol County Planning and Development
text:
# Unpermitted Structure Legalization (unincorporated county)

The Planning and Development Department administers legalization of unpermitted dwelling units and accessory structures in the unincorporated area under Marisol Government Code section 41210 and County Code Title 22, Chapter 22.190. This program does not apply inside city limits; if your property is in Halvern or Ardenmoor, contact that city.

## Requirements

1. Pre-application research request ($75) so staff can pull the parcel's permit history.
2. Application on Form PDD-88 with the legalization fee of $610, existing-condition plans, and a site plan stamped by a licensed surveyor where the parcel exceeds one acre.
3. **Onsite wastewater evaluation.** Parcels on septic must submit an evaluation by a qualified professional showing the system has capacity for the additional unit. Environmental Health review of the evaluation is a separate submittal and is the most common source of delay.
4. Fire district clearance for parcels in a high fire hazard severity zone, including defensible space verification.
5. Building plan review and inspection.
6. Issuance of a Certificate of Legal Nonconforming Status.

## Timeline

Typical processing is 90 to 120 days. Files requiring a new septic design routinely exceed six months. The county does not offer a third-party inspection option.

Questions: pdd-legalization@marisolcounty.gov
